The most recent source says Neon's free storage limit has doubled, while the pricing pages still show the older 0.5 GB figure.

The search results mostly agree that PlanetScale Postgres has no free tier. The cheapest option is a paid plan starting at $5/month.

- **No free tier (majority view):** Several sources say PlanetScale dropped its free Hobby plan in April 2024 and has not reinstated it. One lists the self-serve Base plan at $5/month, and another notes that a single-node PS-5 is the cheapest real entry point.
- **Paid tiers:** The Base plan launched in October 2025 for single-node, non-HA Postgres. Pricing is resource-based and billed by the millisecond. HA 3-node clusters cost roughly three times the single-node price (for example, $30/month for PS-10 HA versus $10 single-node).
- **Conflicting source:** Two CostBench pages (one dated 2026) describe a "free" plan, but their own tier lists omit it. Other CostBench pages say there is no free tier, so I'd treat the free-plan claim as unreliable.
- **Free alternatives:** Neon and Supabase both offer free Postgres tiers, and sources cite Neon's 0.5 GB free tier and Supabase's 500 MB free tier.

I didn't check PlanetScale's official pricing page, so confirm current plans there before relying on these figures.

The free tier's 500 MB database cap and one-week inactivity pause are consistent across the sources, though some details differ.

- **Database cap:** The official Supabase pricing page lists 500 MB of database space on the Free plan, along with 50,000 monthly active users, 5 GB of bandwidth, and 1 GB of file storage Get started with: - Unlimited API requests - 50,000 monthly active users - 500 MB database space. A Medium guide says exceeding that limit puts the database into read-only mode, attributing this to Supabase's documentation when you exceed this limit, your database enters read-only mode to prevent further data insertion. I could not confirm that behavior in the official docs from these results, so treat it as unverified.
- **Project limit:** The Free plan allows two active projects Limit of 2 active projects.
- **Pausing:** Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. A paused project keeps its data, but it stays offline until someone restores it from the dashboard the app goes dark until someone manually restores it from the dashboard.
- **Upgrade path:** Pro removes the pausing behavior and raises the database to 8 GB, with usage overages billed beyond the included quotas. One source notes Pro plan: 8 GB database space then $0.125 per GB.
- **Discrepancy:** Some third-party guides list file storage as 500 MB on Free, while the official page and others say 1 GB. The official figure is more reliable.

content.text:
PlanetScale has no free Postgres tier. Neon and Supabase do. I couldn't open any pricing page directly (every fetch was refused by the proxy), so these numbers come from web-search summaries, not from the official pages. Please check them against the official pages before relying on them.

| | **Neon Free** | **Supabase Free** | **PlanetScale** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier? | Yes | Yes | No |
| Storage | 1 GB per project (was 0.5 GB) | 500 MB database | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month, autoscaling up to 2 CU | Not found | n/a |
| Idle behavior | Scales to zero after 5 minutes, and wakes on the next connection | Project paused after 1 week of inactivity, restored manually from the dashboard | n/a |
| Projects | 100 projects, 10 branches per project | 2 active projects | n/a |
| Egress | 5 GB per month | 5 GB bandwidth | n/a |
| Other | Compute suspends when you hit a monthly limit, until the next billing month | 50,000 monthly active users (MAU), 1 GB file storage, unlimited API requests | Cheapest option is the $5/month Base plan (single node, no high availability) |

**Sources**
- **Neon:**
  - The 1 GB storage figure comes from Neon's blog post, ["Just shipped"](https://neon.com/blog/neon-free-plan-1-gb-per-project). It is the newest source I found.
  - The 100 CU-hours, 100 projects, 10 branches, 5 GB egress and 5-minute scale-to-zero figures come from the search summary of Neon's [pricing page](https://neon.com/pricing) and its [free-tier FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/managed-postgres-databases-free-tier).
  - The summary said the limit-suspension behavior came from an article that predates the 1 GB change. Most other pages still list 0.5 GB.
- **Supabase:**
  - The 500 MB, 50,000 MAU, 5 GB bandwidth and 1 GB file storage figures are attributed to the [official pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing), seen only through a search summary.
  - The 2-project limit and 1-week pause come from third-party guides, such as [Jetadmin's 2026 guide](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/supabase-pricing-2026-guide-to-plans-limits-and-real-world-costs/).
  - Some guides say file storage is 500 MB. I used the official 1 GB figure.
  - One Medium guide says the database goes read-only when it exceeds 500 MB. I couldn't confirm that in the official docs.
- **PlanetScale:**
  - Several third-party sources, such as [Bytebase's comparison](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/) and [CostBench](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/), say the free Hobby plan was dropped in April 2024 and not brought back.
  - The $5/month Base plan, launched in October 2025, comes from those same secondary sources.
  - Two CostBench pages claim a free plan, but their own tier lists don't include one, so I discounted them.

**Summary:** Neon's free tier suits intermittent use, since compute scales to zero and storage is larger. Supabase's is smaller on storage and pauses idle projects, but it bundles auth, file storage and APIs. On PlanetScale, plan on paying at least $5/month.
